body:
## Problem
The CPU renderer gives a Fit image fill (and a Crop whose frame leaves the picture) a transparent border by copying the whole decoded picture into a new pixmap one pixel larger on each side, on every paint call (`crates/designos-render/src/paint.rs`, the `padded` pixmap in the image branch of `with_paint`). A 4032x3024 photo in Fit costs about 49 MB of allocation and copy for each tile that draws it. If that allocation fails, the `?` drops the fill without a trace.

## Expected
Drawing a Fit or out-of-bounds Crop fill does work bounded by the visible region, the letterbox stays transparent, and a failed allocation draws something and is counted, not dropped.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test renders a 64x64 region of a 4000x3000 Fit fill and shows no full-picture allocation (instrumented behind `cfg(test)`).
- [ ] The letterbox stays transparent; CPU vs GPU parity tests for Fit and Crop stay green.
- [ ] Release timing of one 256x256 tile over a 4032x3024 Fit fill at dpr 2, before and after, in the PR.

## Notes
The adjusted-image path in #163's PR samples into a bounded scratch and no longer needs the copy; this issue covers the plain (unadjusted) path, which must keep its pixels unless the PR shows and explains any difference.
title: CPU Fit image fills copy the whole picture on every paint
